lessonRef.title: Performance task build: evidence-based collegial seminar

studentTask.text: Today's focus: evidence-based collegial seminar. Essential question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to evidence-based collegial seminar change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Explain what evidence-based collegial seminar means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play. You'll need: course notebook or digital equivalent; the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation; citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Plan check: Re-read the plan of record. Name what changed since planning and why.
- Sustained production: Uninterrupted work on Write and present a comparative analysis of a world-literature text and a later work that transforms it.. The learner produces; the tutor is available for questions and critique but writes nothing that will be assessed.
- Self-critique against criteria: Compare the work in progress against the success criteria and mark the weakest section.
- Access and source check: Confirm every text the build depends on is still available in an accessible representation and that nothing required sits behind a rights barrier.
- Next-session commitment: Record exactly where work will resume.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for today's lesson, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
- If repeated error pattern: Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of today's lesson.
- If procedure without understanding: Ask the learner to explain why the move for today's lesson works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
